extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers of the GAP computer algebra system (mathematicians, computational algebraists, package authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for installing, using, reporting bugs, citing, and developing extensions (packages) for the GAP computer algebra system; aimed at both end-users and contributors. Covers distribution/licensing, package structure and loading, documentation formats, and community/support procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: GAP distribution conditions (free/open)
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP is a free, open and extensible software package for computation in discrete abstract algebra. The terms free and open describe the conditions under which the system is distributed -- in brief, it is free of charge (except possibly for the immediate costs of delivering it to you), you are free to pass it on within certain limits, and all of the workings of the system are open for you to examine and change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details of these conditions can be found in Section Reference: Copyright and License.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensibility and contribution of GAP packages
rubrics_metrics.description: The system is extensible in that you can write your own programs in the GAP language, and use them in just the same way as the programs which form part of the system (the library). We actively support the contribution, refereeing and distribution of extensions to the system, in the form of GAP packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further details can be found in Chapter Reference: Using and Developing GAP Packages, and on the GAP website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package contents and permitted contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A package contains GAP code and its own documentation and may also contain data files or external programs to which the GAP code provides an interface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Packages are self-contained extensions and may include data files or external programs; they should provide their own documentation (manuals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Loading packages into GAP
rubrics_metrics.description: These packages may be loaded into GAP using the LoadPackage (Reference: LoadPackage) command, and both the package and its documentation are then available just as if they were parts of the core system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some packages may be loaded automatically when GAP is started if present. See the LoadPackage reference for exact usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: OS and external-dependency limitations for packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Some packages, because they depend on external programs, may only be available on the operating systems where those programs are available (usually UNIX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that package availability can be OS-dependent; consult package documentation and the website for platform support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to install and use packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Other packages contain functionality which has never been part of the core system, and may extend it substantially, implementing specific algorithms to enhance its capabilities, providing data libraries, interfaces to other computer algebra systems and data sources; therefore, installation and usage of packages is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Packages can substantially extend GAP's capabilities; users are encouraged to install relevant packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation formats and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The documentation. This is available as on-line help, as printable files in PDF format and as HTML for viewing with a Web browser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Package documentation is likewise provided as manuals; use the online/manual/HTML formats according to preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to prepare a useful bug report / support request
rubrics_metrics.description: Please give a (short, if possible) self-contained excerpt of a GAP session containing both input and output that illustrates your problem (including comments of why you think it is a bug) and state the type of the machine, operating system, (compiler used, if UNIX/Linux) and the version of GAP you are using (the first line after the GAP 4 banner starting GAP, Version 4...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send such reports to support@gap-system.org for issues not suitable for the public forum; include concrete session excerpts and system/version details to expedite diagnosis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the GAP Forum and subscription requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The GAP Forum – an email discussion forum for comments, discussions or questions about GAP. You must subscribe to the list before you can post to it, see the website for details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The forum is used for announcements (e.g., new releases) and community discussion; follow subscription rules on the website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify support when you install GAP
rubrics_metrics.description: We also ask you to send a brief message to support@gap-system.org when you install GAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A brief installation message helps the maintainers; include relevant platform/version information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct citation of GAP in publications
rubrics_metrics.description: The correct form of citation of GAP, which we ask you use whenever you publish scientific results obtained using GAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the manual or website for the exact citation format and use it in scientific publications that used GAP results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core system components and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: The core system consists of: a kernel (written in C) providing automatic dynamic storage management and time-critical basic functions; an interpreter for the GAP language; a small set of system functions for files and external programs; a set of programming tools for testing, debugging, and timing algorithms; a read-eval-view style user interface; a much larger library of GAP functions implementing algorithms (written in GAP language); a library of group theoretical data; and documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding these components clarifies where to implement extensions (in packages or library), and why much of the library is written in GAP so users can inspect and modify algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for moving functionality into packages
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two packages (the library of ordinary and Brauer character tables, and the library of tables of marks) which contain functionality developed from parts of the GAP core system. These have been moved into packages for ease of maintenance and to allow new versions to be released independently of new releases of the core system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When developing features, consider packaging them if independent release/maintenance is desirable.
